title: Vivarium per-recipe metadata (schema_version 1)
description: Per-recipe metadata sibling of a recipe's tracked sources (README.md / repro.* / index.html / Dockerfile) under src/layer{1,2,3}_*/<slug>/recipe.json. Single source of truth for the facets the gallery filters on (language / symptom / severity / tags) and the expectations the regression suite will assert (expected_verdict / expected_runtime). Replaces the hand-curated overlay at docs/site/_data/recipe-facets.json (retired 2026-05-18). Consumed by docs/scripts/generate-recipes-index.ts (merges the fields into the public docs/site/public/api/recipes.json catalogue), by src/layer1_wasm/scripts/highlight-repros.ts (reads language to pick the Shiki bundle), and by src/layer1_wasm/tests/repro.spec.ts via the generated catalogue (reads expected_verdict / expected_runtime for the regression suite). Adding a new recipe = creating its directory + this file; the projects.json overlay remains the only out-of-recipe edit, and only when a new project debuts.

schema_version.description: Schema version literal. Always 1 for files validating against this schema; breaking changes ship as a sibling schema (recipe.v2.schema.json) per ADR-0018.

language.description: Primary source language of the reproduction. Layer 1 uses the value to pick a Shiki bundle for syntax highlighting (so the value must be a Shiki BundledLanguage ID such as 'python', 'ruby', 'php', 'rust', 'javascript', 'shell', 'sql', 'c'); Layer 2/3 only use it for gallery filtering. 'unknown' is allowed as a degraded default but should be replaced as soon as a maintainer can label the recipe.

symptom.description: Short kebab-case label for the bug shape (e.g. 'dtype-mismatch', 'lost-update-data-race'). Surfaced in the gallery as a facet; the value space is intentionally open — pick the most descriptive existing tag if possible, coin a new one if not.

severity.description: Short label for the bug's severity class (e.g. 'bug', 'regression', 'spec-violation', 'footgun', 'datarace'). Surfaced as a gallery facet. Like symptom, intentionally open — see existing recipe.json files for the value space in use.

tags.description: Free-form tags surfaced in the gallery filter chips. Conventionally includes the upstream project name, the language feature involved, and any relevant standards or libraries. Order is preserved as authored.

expected_verdict.description: Verdict the regression suite (src/layer1_wasm/tests/repro.spec.ts and equivalents) expects the recipe page to produce. Currently 'reproduced' for every shipped recipe — when an upstream fix lands and the runtime picks it up, the suite turns the flip into a CI failure so a maintainer can decide whether to update / retire the recipe. Required in practice for Layer 1 / Layer 2 recipes: src/layer1_wasm/tests/repro.spec.ts refuses to start when the field is missing or off-enum. Schema keeps it optional so external_examples and future layers can ship recipe.json without owning this field; ADR-0018 spec evolution policy reserves required-promotion for v2.

expected_runtime.description: Runtime identifier the recipe's verdict envelope reports in `__VIVARIUM_RESULT__.runtime.name`. For Layer 1: 'pyodide' / 'ruby.wasm' / 'php-wasm' / 'rust-wasi' / 'terrarium' / 'browser' (the smoke test). For Layer 2: 'docker-snapshot'. Layer 3 ships no recipes, so it has no established value. Asserted by the regression suite alongside expected_verdict, and required in practice on the same terms: src/layer1_wasm/tests/repro.spec.ts refuses to start when the value is missing or unrecognised.

path_a.description: Whether the recipe page mounts the Path A "Try a fix" panel (enablePathA). Layer 1 only; absent means no.

upstream.description: The released upstream version the recipe's baseline runs, for recipes whose baseline is pinned to an upstream release rather than to a runtime's bundled copy. Layer 1 only. The upstream-bump workflow compares it with the upstream's latest release every day and, when they differ, opens a pull request that moves the pin everywhere it appears in the recipe's non-Markdown files; that pull request's regression run then shows whether the bug still reproduces on the new release.

version.description: Pinned release, exactly as written in the recipe's files.

repository.description: owner/name of the GitHub repository whose latest release is tracked.

commit.description: Commit the tag points to; the recipe fetches this commit.

upstream_pr.description: The upstream pull request that fixes the bug, for recipes that do not use fix-candidate.json (whose upstream_pr plays the same role). The retire-merged workflow checks it every day and, once it is merged, opens a pull request that removes the recipe.

fix_candidate.description: The branch a Layer 1 recipe's fix-candidate pane builds from source, pinned to a commit, for recipes that do not use fix-candidate.json (whose source.commit plays the same role for fork wheels). The upstream-bump workflow compares the pin with the branch head every day and, when they differ, opens a pull request that moves the commit, and its first eight characters, everywhere they appear in the recipe's non-Markdown files.

repository.description: owner/name of the GitHub repository holding the branch.

branch.description: Branch the fix is developed on, usually the head of the upstream pull request.
